summary: Defect-repair dispatch (not a plan phase). Verified Phase 12's own diagnosis against the recovered source PDF directly (pages 6, 9, 10 rendered) rather than assuming it: the diagnosis was CONFIRMED but the conclusion is SHARPER than Phase 12 anticipated. Both `id` and `orL` (`∨•`) -- not just `id` -- were over-generalized in Rules.lean (Phase 9): they were encoded via `InputCtx.fillLhs` (an arbitrary `Γ'`/`Λ` split with a companion `π`), but Figure 2 writes both rules with the companion output formula INSIDE THE SAME BRACES as the principal formula (`Γ{a•,a°}`, `Γ{A•,Π°}`), and Lemma 4.2 (`id`)/Lemma 4.8-4.9 (`orL`) make explicit that `Γ{ }` here is an OUTPUT context filled via `.fillFull`, not an input context with a genuinely-nested `Λ`. The `InputCtx.fillLhs` reading is strictly more general than the paper's own rule, and that extra generality is exactly what manufactured the apparent obstruction (a spurious, unremovable diamond past `Λ`-depth 1). Repaired both constructor signatures in Rules.lean to use `OutputCtx.fillFull`. Both sorries then closed IMMEDIATELY from already-landed Phase-11 lemmas (`lemma4_2_id` for `id`; `lemma4_8` plus one new closed or-elimination schema for `orL`) -- no `kdisj`, no new axiom, no diamond ever appears in either proof (both `.fillFull`'s and `lemma4_8`'s recursions are box-only throughout). `botL` (`⊥•`) has the identical mismatch but was left untouched: its extra generality stays TRUE (bot trivially implies everything via `efq` regardless of `◇`-wrapping depth), so it is a stronger-but-still-sound theorem, not a defect -- not in scope, not touched. Verified Phases 9-12 all stay green: full `lake build` (3258/3259, no errors), `lake test` (9252/9253, no errors), `lake lint`/`lake exe lint-style` (no Nested/ complaints), `lake exe checkInitImports` (exit 0), `lake exe mk_all --module` (no update necessary), scoped `lake shake` (only the known `Cslib.Init` false positive). Axiom count unchanged at 26; no new axioms; `#print axioms nested_sound_id` reports none, `#print axioms nested_sound_orL` reports only the standard Mathlib meta-axioms (propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound), not a new CSLib axiom.
research_finding_bearing_on_task_554: This finding is UNRELATED to (and does not weaken) the task's central disjunction-property obstruction. The `orL` sorry's apparent need for `kdisj` (`◇(A∨B) ⊃ (◇A∨◇B)`) was an ARTIFACT of the over-general `InputCtx` encoding, not a genuine recurrence of the box-over-disjunction wall (`□(A∨B) ⊃ (□A∨□B)`) that is the documented central obstruction elsewhere in this task and in the independent labelled-CS5 formalization front. These are different schemas: the diamond-dual `◇(A∨B)⊃(◇A∨◇B)` IS classically valid (via De Morgan + box-and-distribution) and only fails intuitionistically without `kdisj`; the box schema `□(A∨B)⊃(□A∨□B)` fails even classically (already-documented, unrelated to constructivity). With this repair, `orL`'s soundness at the paper's own intended generality is now a clean, sorry-free `CS5` theorem needing no `kdisj` at all -- so this was a FALSE ALARM from a Lean-encoding bug on a third front, now resolved, not a third independent hit of the same wall. The genuine box-over-disjunction obstruction (Stage G's central risk, Phases 26-32) is completely untouched by this finding.

orL's repaired signature: (ctx : OutputCtx Atom) (A B : Proposition Atom) (π : NestedRhs Atom) -> two fillFull-shaped premises -> fillFull-shaped conclusion (spelled lowercase π, per the codebase's standing capital-Pi-is-unusable convention). Closes via lemma4_8 (already landed) instantiated with a new closed schema cs5DerivOrElimSchema : ⊢ ((A⊃C)∧(B⊃C))⊃((A∨B)⊃C), matching Lemma 4.9's own cited propositional fact verbatim.

botL is intentionally NOT repaired: same InputCtx-vs-OutputCtx mismatch relative to Lemma 4.2's minimal scope, but the extra generality remains true (efq makes bot absorb any diamond-wrapping), so nested_sound_botL's existing proof stands unchanged as a valid, stronger theorem. This is a generalization, not a defect, and repairing it was outside this dispatch's scope.

The height function, NestedProof.mono/.mono_height, and the two Rules.lean smoke-test examples were updated to match the new id/orL arities; no other file in the repository references these two constructors (confirmed via repo-wide grep), so blast radius was confined to Rules.lean and Soundness.lean.
